samples.summary: The tightened PUT validator (`depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) rejects documents the new producer caps deliberately allow — it counts *every* block, not just tables, so content one level inside the deepest legal table is a 400
samples.evidence:
`assertValidBlock` recurses into cell blocks with `depth + 1` (docs-content.controller.ts:499-503) and now throws at `depth >= 32`. But the other producers this change added stop one level shallower in *table* terms: `DocxImporter.convertTable` keeps a table whenever `depth + 1 < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:~435), so its worst case is tables at model depths 0…31 whose cell blocks sit at depth 32; `writeDocsRoot`/`buildBlockNode` happily write that (only *tables* at depth>=32 are refused), and `treeNodeToBlock` reads it back in full. The editor's own guard is the same: `editor.ts:4232` refuses an insert only when `tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) >= 32`, so a caret at depth 31 legally creates a table at depth 31 with blocks at 32.
Broken out-of-diff sites: (1) `packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:181` (`client.putDocContent(replace, doc)`) — a .docx with >=31 nested tables now imports fine locally and then 400s on PUT with "blocks are nested too deeply", failing the whole CLI import; (2) the documented GET→edit→PUT identity (see the comment at docs-content.controller.ts:421) — `GET /content` of an editor-produced document with a table at depth 31 returns blocks at depth 32, and PUTing it back unchanged is now a 400.

samples.summary: `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` can now throw, but every out-of-diff caller reaches them through `Doc` mutators that never threw before (and `MemDocStore` still never throws), so the new refusal surfaces as an uncaught exception mid-command
samples.evidence: The new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` gate in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1829` (updateBlock) and :3020 (updateTableCell) throws a raw `Error`. Callers are unguarded: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185` (`this.doc.updateBlockDirect(cr.blockId, block)` on the cell-rectangle delete path) and the ~30 `Doc` mutators in `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts` that delegate to `store.updateBlock`/`store.updateTableCell`. None catches, and `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts) has no equivalent throw, so the `DocStore` contract in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:23/102 now differs per implementation and code written against the in-package store passes there and throws under the collaborative one. Reachable only on a document that already holds rows past the cap, which is why confidence is low — but the throw escapes a keystroke/command handler when it happens.

samples.summary: Template seeding calls the now-throwing `writeDocsRoot` with no handling, so a seed whose docs content reaches the nesting cap aborts seeding with a raw Error instead of a validation message
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/template/seed/seed-templates.ts:79` — `doc.update((root) => writeDocsRoot(root, content.document));`. `writeDocsRoot` now throws `refusing to rewrite the document: …` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:376). Unlike the PUT endpoint (400) and the copy service (BadRequestException), this path has no guard or classification, and seed content is not run through `assertValidDocsBody`.

samples.summary: The `Math.max(...rows.map(...))` RangeError hazard the diff fixed in `range-slices.ts` and `selection.ts` is left in place at three clipboard sites and in the markdown serializer
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:323 (`sanitizeTableData`, over an untrusted clipboard payload), :891, :971, :1055, and packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:180 all still spread a peer/clipboard-chosen row array into `Math.max`, the exact pattern the diff replaced with a fold at packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:57 and packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:208 with the comment "throws `RangeError` past ~100k arguments, and the row count is a peer's to choose". These sites still work today but are now out of step with the stated invariant.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: assertValidBlock rejects any block (not just tables) at depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH=32 (docs-content.controller.ts:454, recursion at :499-503, entry at :191/:316/:350), while every other producer/reader in the repo permits tables at depth 0..31 and therefore ordinary blocks at depth 32: buildBlockNode/hasDocsTableAtNestingCap only cap *tables* (docs-tree.ts:179,237), treeNodeToBlock only truncates *tables* at depth>=32 (crdt-tree.ts:225) so GET returns depth-32 blocks, DocxImporter keeps nested tables while depth+1 < 32 (docx-importer.ts:437), and the editor refuses insertion only at tableNestingDepth>=32 (editor.ts:4232 with semantics at document.ts:158-170). Concrete out-of-diff breakage: CLI import PUTs importer output at packages/cli/src/docs/import.ts:181 (would now 400 "blocks are nested too deeply"), and the documented GET->edit->PUT identity (contract stated at docs-content.controller.ts:418-427, GET at :139) fails for an editor-produced document with a table at depth 31. This is a changed contract with unupdated producers/consumers outside the diff — in lane, major.

finding.evidence: The new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` gate in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1829` (updateBlock) and :3020 (updateTableCell) throws a raw `Error`. Callers are unguarded: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185` (`this.doc.updateBlockDirect(cr.blockId, block)` on the cell-rectangle delete path) and the ~30 `Doc` mutators in `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts` that delegate to `store.updateBlock`/`store.updateTableCell`. None catches, and `MemDocStore` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts) has no equivalent throw, so the `DocStore` contract in packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:23/102 now differs per implementation and code written against the in-package store passes there and throws under the collaborative one. Reachable only on a document that already holds rows past the cap, which is why confidence is low — but the throw escapes a keystroke/command handler when it happens.

verdict.reason: The described code exists and the callers are genuinely unguarded. `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1833-1835) and `updateTableCell` (:3021-3026) now call `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows`, which throws a raw Error (:1752, constructed at :503-509). Out-of-diff callers do not catch: `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:793-794` (`updateBlockDirect`), :955, :1155, :1184; and `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4185` invokes `updateBlockDirect` mid-command with cursor/markDirty/requestRender work following at :4187-4194, so a throw aborts the command handler (the file's only catches are at :1628, :3027, :4503, :6246, :6268 and none covers this call). The `DocStore` interface documents these as plain `void` (store.ts:23, :102) and explicitly documents throw parity only for `batch()` (:62-85), while `MemDocStore` (memory.ts:91, :374) has no equivalent refusal — its throws are structural only (:123, :426, :429, :545). So a contract change (newly thrown error) has unupdated callers, which is squarely in the blast-radius lane. Reachability requires a document already holding rows past MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH=32 (table-nesting.ts:26), which the finding itself flags as the low-confidence part; that affects confidence, not whether the bypassing/broken site is real. No guard, catch, or precondition check exists that would make the throw unreachable, so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: The new `updateTableCell` / `updateBlock` truncated-rows refusal is gated on the *replacement* model, so every writer that replaces a cell/block with content that contains no table-at-cap walks straight past it and still deletes the peer rows the reader never read
finding.evidence:
The gate added in `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3021` (`if (hasTableAtNestingCap(cell.blocks, rowDepth)) this.assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows(...)`) and its twin at `yorkie-doc-store.ts:1831` only consult the tree when the *new* model still carries a table at the cap. Out-of-diff callers replace cells/blocks with content that has none:
- `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1137,1155` — `Doc.mergeCells` resets every covered cell to a single empty paragraph and then `store.updateTableCell(blockId, r, c, ...)` for the whole rectangle. The covered cell's model has no table at the cap, so the guard is never asked, and the cell node in the CRDT — which may hold a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with rows this reader truncated — is replaced whole. The rows a peer wrote are deleted and replicated, which is exactly the outcome the new refusal exists to prevent. (The top-left cell, which *does* get a table-at-cap in its model, is checked against its own path, which holds nothing truncated, so it passes and then writes the table back rowless.)
- `packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1183-1184` — `Doc.splitCell` does the same for restored covered cells.
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4177-4185` — the cell-range delete clears cells then `updateBlockDirect(cr.blockId, block)`; a user-intended delete, but it reaches `updateBlock` with the gate false as well, confirming the gate's shape rather than its intent is what decides.
The fix belongs on the new code: the tree check has to be driven by what is at the target path, not by what the caller is about to write (cheap pre-filter could be the old node, not the new model).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: the new refusal in `updateTableCell` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3021-3026) and `updateBlock` (1833-1835) is gated on `hasTableAtNestingCap` over the *replacement* model, and the only tree-side check (`treeHasTruncatedRows` via `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows`, 1748-1753) sits behind that gate, while the replacement itself (editByPath at 3033-3037 / 1847) is unconditional. Out-of-diff callers replace cells/blocks with content containing no table at the cap and therefore never trigger the check: `Doc.mergeCells` resets covered cells to a single empty paragraph (document.ts:1137) and then calls `store.updateTableCell` for every cell in the rectangle (document.ts:1155); `Doc.splitCell` does the same (document.ts:1183-1184); the cell-range delete in text-editor.ts:4177-4185 clears cells then calls `updateBlockDirect` -> `updateBlock`. Each of these replaces the CRDT node whole, so rows a peer wrote at or past MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH — rows this reader truncated at read time — are deleted and replicated, precisely the outcome the new guard exists to prevent. No caller-side or model-side guard elsewhere blocks these paths.

finding.summary: Dropping the merge-expansion budget from `normalizeCellRange`'s default makes `Selection.getNormalizedRange` unbounded for callers that neither paint nor write — including a per-keystroke arrow-key path
finding.evidence:
`normalizeCellRange`/`normalizeRange` now default `budgetCells = Infinity` and only `computeSelectionRects` (selection.ts:715) passes `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`. The new comments justify this by saying every remaining `getNormalizedRange` caller *acts* on the rectangle, but two out-of-diff callers do not:
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3378` — plain Left/Right/Up/Down with a selection collapses it via `getNormalizedRange`, using only `normalized.start`/`end`. This runs on every such keystroke and now pays the unbounded fixed-point expansion (superlinear in a peer-chosen row count) that the budget was introduced to bound.
- `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:501` — `formatSourcePosition()` (format painter, reached from `copyFormat()` at line 467) likewise only reads the ordered rectangle.
Neither writes anything, so the "a short rectangle corrupts a merge" rationale does not apply to them; they get the hang risk with none of the benefit. Fix belongs on the new code (pass a budget from these read-only callers, or keep the default budgeted and opt the writers out).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: expandCellRangeForMerges/normalizeCellRange/normalizeRange all default budgetCells = Infinity (selection.ts:126, 205, 265), and the only budgeted call site in the whole repository is computeSelectionRects at selection.ts:715; Selection.getNormalizedRange (selection.ts:901-906) passes no budget. The new rationale comments (selection.ts:26-36 and 254-260) assert that every getNormalizedRange caller "acts on" the rectangle (clear/copy/cut), but text-editor.ts:499-541 formatSourcePosition() calls getNormalizedRange at line 501 and handles normalized.tableCellRange at 506-513 by reading only rect.start.rowIndex/colIndex — a pure read, reached from copyFormat() at text-editor.ts:467 (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+C and the toolbar toggle). That read-only consumer now pays the unbounded superlinear merge expansion over a peer-chosen table size with none of the correctness benefit the comment cites. The second cited site (text-editor.ts:3375-3385) is weaker than claimed — an in-cell caret is diverted by arrowCellInfo at text-editor.ts:3043-3044 into the in-table branch, which returns at 3348 after setRange(null) at 3343 without normalizing — but I could not establish that tableCellRange is never set while the caret is outside a cell (e.g. editor.ts:2486-2497 restores a range carrying tableCellRange verbatim), so that site is not ruled out either. No refutation ground holds: the code is present as described, no guard makes the format-painter path unreachable with a cell rectangle, and a behaviour change to a shared helper affecting unconsidered out-of-diff consumers is squarely in the blast-radius lane at major severity.
